Step-by-Step Guide

Tap any step timer to launch Cook Mode right there

restaurant_menu
1

Simmer & Dissolve Smoothly

Heat the oven to 180°C. For the dough, mix flour and sugar in a bowl. Heat the 100 grams of milk to lukewarm and dissolve the yeast in it. Let stand for a while until it starts to bubble. Then add to the flour along with the coconut oil and mix into a smooth dough. Let rise for 30 minutes, covered, in a warm place. Incorporate 7/8 cup flour, 5 tbsp coconut oil, 6 2/3 tbsp vegetable millk, and 2 tsp yeast smoothly until evenly distributed.

lightbulb
Creator Secret

Prep and measure flour first—mise en place makes this dessert twice as fast.

2

Simmer & Dissolve Smoothly

Meanwhile, make the rice pudding by putting the rice with sugar, milk and vanilla extract in a saucepan. Add the cardamom, star anise and cinnamon. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring constantly. Take out the spices. In a small bowl, mix baking soda with lemon juice/apple vinegar. Stir well until baking soda is dissolved, then mix into the rice pudding. Incorporate 3 1/3 tbsp sugar, 10 tbsp dessert rice, and 6 2/3 tbsp sugar smoothly until evenly distributed.

3

Combine Wet & Dry Smoothly

Fold 3 1/8 cup vegetable millk, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 whole cardamom, 2 whole star anise, 1 whole cinnamon stick, 1/2 tsp baking powder, and 1/2 tsp lemon juice into the base in two additions using gentle strokes until glossy and uniform with zero dry pockets. Avoid overmixing so the final texture stays light and tender.

4

Shape & Press Dough Evenly

Roll out the dough on a floured work surface (it is very sticky, but don’t stress it will be fine) and line the bottom and edges of a greased mold with it. Spread the rice pudding over the bottom and bake for about 25 to 30 minutes.

lightbulb
Creator Secret

Chill the filled crust 10 minutes before baking—cold butter hits the hot oven and puffs into extra-flaky layers.

ac_unit

Let set for 5–10 minutes before slicing or plating so the textures hold crisp and photogenic!

Nutrition, Storage & Healthy Prep Notes

CALORIES410 kcal
SERVINGS6
SUGAR MODEClassic

Make-Ahead & Storage: Keep traditional dutch rice tart (rijstevlaai) in an airtight glass container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days (or freeze individual portions up to 1 month). Pair with unsweetened Greek yogurt, fresh berries, or espresso for a balanced treat.

Keto & Low-Sugar Tip: Toggle Healthy Swap above to substitute refined sugar with monk fruit or coconut sugar and white flour with oat or almond flour.
